content.summary: Welcome to the reading mission for Unit B1.2-M05. In this lesson, you will explore how people talk about international dishes, cooking methods, and heritage recipes. You will also practice reading strategies to find specific details about dietary requirements and polite restaurant requests.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Polite indirect questions using 'Could you tell me...' and modal verbs for requests.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Descriptive food adjectives and cooking verbs such as savory, zesty, tender, and simmer.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts quickly to locate specific vocabulary words and details without reading every single word.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short texts about international culinary traditions.
Locate specific details regarding dietary restrictions and food allergies in restaurant reviews.
Recognize and practice polite phrasing for ordering food and making special requests.

contextWarmup.prompt: When you go to a restaurant with new friends, what is the best way to ask about the ingredients in a dish if you have a food allergy?
options: Could you tell me what ingredients are in this dish, please?
What is in this food right now?
Tell me everything you put in here immediately.
contextWarmup.explanation: Option 1 uses polite indirect question structures ('Could you tell me...'), which are standard and polite in English-speaking restaurants.

rules: Gunakan 'Could you tell me...?' atau 'Would it be possible...?' untuk pertanyaan sopan: 'Could you tell me what ingredients are in this dish?' lebih formal daripada 'What's in this?'
Sampaikan alergi dengan jelas menggunakan 'I have a/an [adjective] allergy to...': 'I have a severe nut allergy' atau 'I'm allergic to shellfish' untuk memastikan keamanan.
Gunakan 'Could I have...?' untuk permintaan modifikasi: 'Could I have the dressing on the side?' atau 'Could I have this without garlic, please?' menunjukkan kesopanan.

Kosakata kuliner tingkat intermediate mencakup: savory (gurih), zesty (segar dan pedas), tender (empuk), simmer (memasak dengan api kecil), garnish (hiasan), marinate (merendam bumbu), bland (hambar), aromatic (harum).

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often translate their native language directly when asking for food changes, which can sound too direct or impolite in English.
commonTrap.wrong: Give me the soup without salt.
commonTrap.correct: Could I have the soup without salt, please?

paragraphs: Exploring global cuisine is one of the best ways to experience different cultures. When you travel, you encounter many aromatic dishes filled with unique spices. For example, traditional meat dishes are often prepared by letting them marinate for hours before they cook. This process ensures the meat becomes wonderfully tender and full of rich flavor.

However, dining out requires clear communication when you have special dietary needs. It is important to inform your server if you have any food allergy. You can use polite phrases like, 'Could you tell me if this meal contains dairy?' Furthermore, asking for simple changes, such as having a zesty dressing served on the side, helps ensure a pleasant and safe dining experience.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Ordering Food and Managing Dietary Needs

content.summary: Listen for specific details when ordering food in a restaurant. Focus on how customers politely state allergies, request ingredient changes, and confirm dietary requirements like halal options.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about ordering food.
Identify details such as allergies, ingredients, and specific preferences.
Notice how words link together in connected speech during polite requests.

keyPhrases.note: Used to inform restaurant staff about dangerous food allergies.

keyPhrases.phrase: Could you tell me what is in this dish?
keyPhrases.meaning: Bisakah Anda memberitahu saya apa isi hidangan ini?
keyPhrases.note: A polite way to ask about ingredients before ordering.

keyPhrases.phrase: Could I have it on the side?
keyPhrases.meaning: Bisakah saya minta itu dipisah di samping?
keyPhrases.note: Used when requesting a side dish or sauce not to be mixed into the main meal.

keyPhrases.phrase: Does your restaurant serve halal meat?
keyPhrases.meaning: Apakah restoran Anda menyajikan daging halal?
keyPhrases.note: A direct and polite question to check meat sourcing.

connectedSpeech.note: The sound 'd' and 'y' blend together to form a 'j' sound.
The article 'the' is reduced to a weak vowel sound.
The final consonant of 'all' links directly to the vowel in 'our'.
Consonants link smoothly to following vowels without pauses.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Global Cuisine and Polite Dietary Preferences

content.summary: Practical guide on writing polite requests for food orders, describing culinary dishes, and stating dietary needs clearly in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Polite Inquiry Formula
blueprintItems.formula: Could you tell me + what/if + subject + verb?
blueprintItems.example: Could you tell me what ingredients are in this soup?

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Dietary Restriction Formula
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + have/has + a/an + [adjective] + allergy to + noun
blueprintItems.example: I have a severe nut allergy.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Modification Request Formula
blueprintItems.formula: Could I have + noun phrase + without + ingredient, please?
blueprintItems.example: Could I have the grilled chicken without garlic, please?

mechanicsRules.rule: Use polite modal verbs instead of direct commands when ordering food or asking questions in a restaurant.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Tell me what is in this dish.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Could you tell me what is in this dish, please?
mechanicsRules.why: Using 'Could you' makes your request much more polite and appropriate for customer service interactions.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize the names of nationalities and specific regional cuisines.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i love italian and mexican food.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I love Italian and Mexican food.
mechanicsRules.why: Nationalities and culinary terms derived from countries are proper adjectives in English.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place adjectives before the noun when describing food textures and flavors.
mechanicsRules.why: In English, descriptive adjectives come before the noun they modify.

sampleSentences.en: Could you tell me if this traditional curry is very spicy?
sampleSentences.id: Bisakah Anda memberitahu saya apakah kari tradisional ini sangat pedas?

sampleSentences.en: I have a strict allergy to peanuts and tree nuts.
sampleSentences.id: Saya memiliki alergi ketat terhadap kacang tanah dan kacang pohon.

sampleSentences.en: Could I have the citrus dressing on the side, please?
sampleSentences.id: Bolehkah saya meminta saus jeruk di mangkuk terpisah, tolong?

sampleSentences.en: The chef decided to marinate the chicken in herbs for two hours.
sampleSentences.id: Koki memutuskan untuk merendam ayam dalam rempah-rempah selama dua jam.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change this direct question into a polite indirect question starting with 'Could you tell me...':

practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Could you tell me what ingredients are in this dessert?'
targetAnswers: Could you tell me what ingredients are in this dessert?
Could you tell me what ingredients are in this dessert
practicumQuestions.explanation: Indirect questions change the word order to subject-verb and remove auxiliary verbs like 'do/does' if present.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence to express a modification request politely using 'Could I have...':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Give me the dressing in a separate bowl.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Could I have the dressing on the side, please?'
targetAnswers: Could I have the dressing on the side, please?
Could I have the dressing in a separate bowl, please?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Polite requests in restaurants use 'Could I have...' followed by the item and 'please'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using 'although':
practicumQuestions.promptText: The soup was very spicy. I enjoyed every single spoonful of it.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Although the soup was very spicy,...'
targetAnswers: Although the soup was very spicy, I enjoyed every single spoonful of it.
Although the soup was very spicy I enjoyed every single spoonful of it.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a contrasting dependent clause, separated by a comma from the main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct all capitalization and punctuation errors in the following sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: i have a severe allergy to peanuts.
targetAnswers: I have a severe allergy to peanuts.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The pronoun 'I' must always be capitalized in English.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence stating that you are allergic to shellfish.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'I have a... allergy to shellfish' or 'I am allergic to...'
targetAnswers: I have a severe allergy to shellfish.
I am allergic to shellfish.
I have an allergy to shellfish.
practicumQuestions.explanation: State food allergies clearly using 'I have a [adjective] allergy to...' or 'I am allergic to...'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change this direct question into an indirect polite question:
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Could you tell me if this dish is vegetarian?'
targetAnswers: Could you tell me if this dish is vegetarian?
Could you tell me whether this dish is vegetarian?
practicumQuestions.explanation: When transforming yes/no questions into indirect questions, use 'if' or 'whether'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the sentences using 'because':
practicumQuestions.promptText: The meat was extremely tender. The chef cooked it slowly for hours.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'because' in the middle of the sentence.
targetAnswers: The meat was extremely tender because the chef cooked it slowly for hours.
The meat was extremely tender because the chef cooked it slowly for several hours.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Because' connects the result clause with the cause clause without needing a comma before it.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the punctuation and capitalization in the following sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: would it be possible to get the steak without sauce please
practicumQuestions.hint: Add a comma before please and a question mark at the end.
targetAnswers: Would it be possible to get the steak without sauce, please?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Questions require a question mark at the end, and sentences must start with a capital letter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a sentence using the culinary adjective 'savory'.
practicumQuestions.hint: Example: 'She prepared a delicious savory pie for dinner.'
targetAnswers: She prepared a delicious savory pie for dinner.
The restaurant serves amazing savory pastries.
I prefer savory dishes over sweet desserts.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Savory' describes food that is salty or spicy rather than sweet.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a polite sentence asking a waiter to remove onions from your meal.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Ask for a meal without onions politely.
targetAnswers: Could I have this meal without onions, please?
Could I have the burger without onions, please?
Could I have my salad without onions, please?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Polite modification requests use 'Could I have...' combined with 'without [ingredient], please'.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Global Cuisine, Culinary Heritage & Expressing Dietary Preferences Politely

content.summary: Master the art of describing global dishes and expressing dietary needs politely in English. Good spoken communication in restaurants relies on clear consonant clusters, accurate syllable stress, and politeintonation patterns.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to word stress in multisyllabic culinary terms like a-ro-MA-tic and DI-et-a-ry. Keep your voice polite and even when making requests.

pillars.name: Culinary Word Stress
pillars.target: Accurate syllable placement in food vocabulary
pillars.explanation: English food words often shift stress to specific syllables, such as MA-ri-nate and GAR-nish. Getting this right ensures clear communication.

pillars.name: Polite Intonation
pillars.explanation: When stating food allergies or asking about ingredients, use a friendly rising-falling intonation pattern to sound polite rather than demanding.

pillars.name: Connected Speech
pillars.explanation: Native speakers link words naturally, such as pronouncing 'could I' as 'coud-I' or 'have a' as 'ha-va' when ordering food.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the stress moves depending on the word structure in food terms.
Both adjectives place strong emphasis on their first syllables.
Health and nutrition words maintain primary stress on the initial syllable.
Cooking terms feature clear trochaic stress patterns.
